items.title: NATIVE: a field read of an operator's result (`(a + b).value`) is refused with "field read of an unresolved subject" - the emitter has no place for the operator call's value
items.discussion: lane solver-56 (Order 56): met while pinning B690's dispatch shapes; JS runs it
items.body: The native emitter resolves a field read's subject to a place or a binding; an overloaded-operator call is neither, so the read fails where a method call's result (`a.add(b).value`) would be a temporary. Rec: treat an operator call as a call expression in `consumed_value_of` (a temporary, like any call) - the same path F153's lane walks. Pin in the native differential. Sizing S.

items.title: std/web/style.vl:243's `root_px_value()` is a B690 workaround (the operator-dispatch miscompile) and its comment is stale now that B690 is fixed - fold it back to the operator form
items.discussion: lane solver-56 (Order 56): B690 2eac7dfd records a call edge per operator dispatch channel, so a module `const let` read through an operator is declared again; the workaround routed the read through a function
items.body: Replace the helper with the operator read it stood in for, drop the comment, confirm the css goldens are byte-identical (the value is const-folded). A lane that is already in style.vl (A178's two, lane std-56 this order) can take it. Sizing XS.

items.title: A path head where an imported MODULE and an imported FUNCTION share a name resolves to the function - `import pkg::editor; import pkg::lib::editor;` then `editor::reader(..)` reads the function and (since E360) says so, where the module was meant
items.status: OPEN - filed 2026-11-03 (lane solver-56's find; lane lang-56's area)
items.discussion: lane solver-56 (Order 56): E360 fa01c52e names the head as a function; the deeper question is that two imports binding one name are not refused at the import, so the later one wins silently
items.body: Either (a) refuse the second import that rebinds a name already bound in the file (the honest rule, as `let` shadowing across imports is already refused for values?), or (b) resolve a `::` path head preferring a MODULE binding when both exist. Rec: (a) - a duplicate import binding is an error with the fix `as`; E360's row then fires only for a genuine function head. Pin both. Sizing S.

items.title: B691's enum copies at std's reactive seams (`releasing_turns.push`, `previous = handle[3].v`, `head = next_same[at]`) cost at run time on JS - a 'never written in place' elision for enums would remove them
items.discussion: lane solver-56 (Order 56): B691 b6c2fa3d makes every enum with a payload an aggregate copied at the rule-1 seams (the copy-elision census 579 -> 612; B509's per-write bound raised 10 -> 20, measured 14); the std reactive core's enum-valued fields are read into bindings in hot paths and never mutated in place there
items.body: Extend the copy-elision rules with an enum-specific case: an enum value read from a place into a binding that is never the subject of a `match &mut`/field write (the only in-place writes an enum admits) needs no copy. The census pins the count; measure on the N186 series (the keystroke rows) before/after. Sizing S-M.
